stemMd: According to the passage, what happens to a careful producer of olive oil when buyers cannot tell good oil from mediocre oil?

options.label: A
options.textMd: It is forced to mix its oil with cheaper stock in order to survive.

options.label: B
options.textMd: It is required to print the harvest date and the name of the mill on its label.

options.label: C
options.textMd: It is paid less than its oil is worth, because buyers offer a price based on the average quality they expect.

options.label: D
options.textMd: It is paid more than its oil is worth, because buyers assume that all green-bottled oil is good.

options.label: E
options.textMd: It is joined by more careful producers, attracted by the price buyers offer.

explanationMd:
Stated-information questions are answered by finding the sentence that says it, then checking that the choice adds nothing. The second paragraph answers this directly: buyers who cannot tell good from mediocre oil offer "a price that reflects the average quality they expect", and a careful producer, whose oil costs more to make than that price repays, "is then paid less than the oil is worth".

Each wrong choice fails a different way. Being paid more than the oil is worth is the reverse of the passage. More careful producers arriving reverses the sequence: the passage says some stop making good oil or leave. Being forced to blend with cheaper stock goes further than the text, which says only that some careful producers stop making the good oil. Printing the harvest date and mill belongs to a later remedy that some cooperatives choose, not a requirement in the market described here.

distractorRationale.a: Blending with cheaper stock appears only in the first paragraph, as one of the things a buyer cannot see. The passage says some careful producers stop making the good oil or leave; it never says they are forced to blend.
distractorRationale.d: The reverse of the passage. Buyers do not assume the best; they discount every bottle, so careful producers are underpaid.
distractorRationale.e: The passage says the opposite: some careful producers stop making good oil or leave the market, and the price offered falls further.
distractorRationale.b: Printing these details is something "some cooperatives" do as a remedy, described in the third paragraph. The passage does not say it is required, nor that it is a consequence of the uninformed market.

accessibilityText: A stated-information question about the olive oil passage. It asks what happens to a careful producer of olive oil when buyers cannot tell good oil from mediocre oil. The five choices say the producer: is forced to mix its oil with cheaper stock to survive; is required to print the harvest date and mill name on its label; is paid less than its oil is worth, because buyers offer a price based on the average quality they expect; is paid more than its oil is worth, because buyers assume all green-bottled oil is good; is joined by more careful producers attracted by the price.

provenance.notes: Original item written for this bank against an original passage. Every option is answerable, or refutable, from the passage text alone.

review.author: tolc-e-wave6-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: This is stated directly: buyers offer a price based on the average quality they expect, so the careful producer 'is then paid less than the oil is worth'. A is not stated, since producers stop making good oil or leave. B is something only some cooperatives do voluntarily. D reverses the passage. E contradicts producers leaving the market. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave6-tolce-verbal-run2) reached the same answer: Paragraph 2 says buyers offer an average-quality price, so the careful producer 'is then paid less than the oil is worth'. A distorts the passage, which says only that some producers stop making good oil or leave. B confuses this with the cooperative remedy, which is voluntary ('Some cooperatives'). D is the opposite of the passage. E is contradicted, because careful producers leave the market.]

review.notes: Uniqueness check: the second paragraph states the correct choice almost verbatim; each other choice is contradicted or not stated. Options were reordered after review to remove answer-position bias; ids and labels were remapped with the key.
